correctness.rationale: For every fixed compact planar convex B with A,P>0 and any apex projection q, the conical ruled surface gives V=Ah/3 and S=A+Ph/2+O(h^-1); the support-function spherical belt estimate gives M=πh+πP/4+O(h^-1). Substitution yields f_h(z)/h=g(z)+k(z)/h+O(h^-2) uniformly on bounded complex z. Two simple limiting roots decide Q<3/4 versus Q>3/4. At Q=3/4, exact k(-P/4π)=P³(3π−13)/(192π²)<0 yields two distinct real roots and the universal h^-1/2 splitting; the third tends to -3h/4 and all real roots are negative. All coefficients, quantifiers and threshold boundary were derived directly. Exact symbolic and independent polyhedral checks in the included script passed; finite tests are only corroboration.

value.rationale: The result is a natural complete eventual root-type classification for arbitrary convex-base three-dimensional pyramids, with a sharp and attained 2D isoperimetric transition and a genuinely nontrivial equality case. It distinguishes all triangular-base pyramids from regular quadrilateral and higher regular polygonal bases at large altitude. Critical root splitting adds a structural law beyond a routine leading-limit discriminant sign; neither the earlier circle special case nor the generic root-classification criterion makes this a trivial restatement.
